title: Grouped Query Experts: MoE Inside Attention
hook: Mixture-of-experts usually routes whole feed-forward layers. Grouped Query Experts routes attention query heads instead — matching a dense baseline while firing half of them per token.
key_points: GQE puts a mixture-of-experts router inside grouped-query attention, picking k query-head experts per token.
Key-value heads stay dense, so the KV-cache savings of GQA are preserved.
Only active query-head computation drops — attention gets sparser without losing its cache benefit.
At 250M params on a fixed 30B-token budget, GQE matched the all-active GQA baseline while activating half the query heads per token.
content_html: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) normally sparsifies the feed-forward layers of a Transformer — a router sends each token to a few expert MLPs. Grouped Query Experts (GQE), from Tripathi and Kumar, applies the same idea somewhere new: inside the attention mechanism, on top of grouped-query attention (GQA).
extra_html:
How it works

Self-attention is often the most expensive part of a Transformer at long context, and standard dense attention applies the same heads to every token regardless of difficulty. GQE adds a router within each GQA group that selects k query-head "experts" per token. Crucially, the key-value (KV) heads stay dense and unchanged, so the model keeps GQA's reduced KV cache; only the active query-head computation goes down.

Why it matters

On a fixed 30B-token budget at the 250M-parameter scale, GQE matched the all-active GQA baseline in downstream accuracy while activating only half the query heads per token. That's the appeal of conditional computation moved into attention: spend attention compute where a token needs it, without sacrificing the cache efficiency that made GQA popular in the first place.

related.title: What Is a Mixture of Experts?
related.hook: Instead of running every input through one big network, route each token to a few specialist sub-networks - total capacity grows without proportional compute.

related.title: Multi-Query Attention: Faster Decoding
related.hook: Share one key/value head across all query heads - the KV cache shrinks by a factor of H and decoding gets dramatically faster with barely any quality cost.

flashcards.prompt: What does Grouped Query Experts make sparse, and what does it keep dense?
flashcards.back_html: It routes (makes sparse) the query-head computation with a per-token expert router, while keeping the key-value heads dense — so GQA's KV-cache savings remain.

flashcards.prompt: Why does GQE keep the key-value heads dense rather than routing them too?

choices.text: To preserve grouped-query attention's reduced KV cache, so only query-head compute is cut
Because routing key-value heads is mathematically impossible
To make the KV cache larger for longer context

flashcards.explanation_html: GQA's whole benefit is a smaller KV cache from sharing key-value heads; GQE leaves that intact and only sparsifies the query-side work.

flashcards.prompt: What was GQE's headline result at the 250M-parameter scale?
flashcards.back_html: It matched the all-active GQA baseline's downstream accuracy while activating only half the query heads per token, on a fixed 30B-token budget.
